skill.name: denario
skill.description: Coordinates multiagent scientific research workflows from dataset description and hypothesis generation through computational analysis and LaTeX manuscript preparation.
skill.summary: Build structured scientific research workflows with generated ideas, methods, results, visualizations, and LaTeX papers.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown syntax, placeholders, or legitimate configuration examples rather than executable threats. Confirmed risks include remote pipe-to-shell installation, credential exposure through shell and container practices, and automated computational execution without documented isolation.

remediation.issue: Remote script is piped directly into bash.
remediation.suggestion: Use a versioned package or download the installer separately, verify its signature and checksum, inspect it, then execute it.

remediation.issue: Mutable containers receive complete environment files and credential mounts.
remediation.suggestion: Pin an image digest, verify its publisher, and provide only required secrets through a dedicated secret manager.

remediation.issue: Troubleshooting prints the complete OpenAI API key.
remediation.suggestion: Check only whether the variable is set and never display its value in terminals, logs, or diagnostics.

remediation.issue: The guide creates and persists long-lived plaintext credentials.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer keyless authentication and session-scoped secrets. Otherwise restrict file permissions, avoid shell profiles, and document rotation.

remediation.issue: Generated research methods can proceed into computational execution.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit approval before execution and run generated work in a sandbox with minimal filesystem, network, and credential access.

content.value_statement: Complex research workflows require coordinated ideation, analysis, literature review, and manuscript preparation. Denario guides a multiagent pipeline from research context to LaTeX paper outputs.
actual_capabilities: Turns dataset and tool descriptions into research hypotheses.
Generates structured methodologies for selected research questions.
Runs computational workflows and produces results and visualizations.
Accepts custom ideas, methodology files, and result files at intermediate stages.
Generates LaTeX manuscripts with supported journal formatting.
Provides command-line and web interface workflows.
limitations: Requires Python 3.12 or later and credentials for an LLM provider.
Paper compilation requires a local LaTeX installation or the documented Docker image.
Available models, journals, and APIs can vary by Denario version.
Generated methods, results, citations, and manuscripts require independent expert validation.

use_cases.title: Develop a Research Plan
use_cases.description: Generate a testable hypothesis and structured methodology from a detailed dataset description.

use_cases.title: Run a Computational Study
use_cases.description: Execute an approved analysis workflow and organize resulting statistics, figures, and limitations.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Draft Manuscript
use_cases.description: Convert reviewed methods and results into a journal-formatted LaTeX paper package.

prompt_templates.title: Generate Research Questions
prompt_templates.prompt: Using this dataset description: [description], propose three testable research questions and explain the strongest choice.
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with a dataset but no defined hypothesis.

prompt_templates.title: Develop a Methodology
prompt_templates.prompt: Develop a reproducible methodology for [hypothesis] using [data and tools], including validation, uncertainty analysis, and expected outputs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Turn an approved hypothesis into an analysis plan.

prompt_templates.title: Execute an Approved Analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Execute the approved methodology in [project directory], generate results and visualizations, and list assumptions, failed checks, and limitations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Produce computational results after reviewing the method.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Controlled Research Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the complete Denario pipeline for [research goal], pausing after every stage for approval and preserving all intermediate artifacts.
prompt_templates.scenario: Coordinate an advanced workflow with human review gates.

output_examples.input: Monthly regional temperature measurements with missing values and seasonal patterns.
output: Research question: Has the long-term warming rate changed after accounting for seasonality?
Recommended method: seasonal decomposition, trend estimation, breakpoint testing, and uncertainty analysis.
Review note: confirm data provenance and missing-value assumptions before execution.

output_examples.input: An approved customer churn methodology using class balancing and cross-validation.
output: Results summary with model metrics and uncertainty.
Visualizations covering discrimination, calibration, and feature importance.
Limitations covering class imbalance, drift, and interpretability.

output_examples.input: Reviewed methods, results, figures, and a request for APS formatting.
output_examples.output: A LaTeX manuscript package containing standard paper sections, integrated figures, references, and journal formatting.

best_practices: Provide data provenance, schema, quality issues, tools, objectives, and constraints before generating ideas.
Review and approve every intermediate artifact before allowing computational execution.
Validate statistics, citations, figures, and claims independently before submission or publication.
anti_patterns: Do not run generated methods against sensitive or production data without isolation and access controls.
Do not treat generated results or citations as verified scientific evidence.
Do not expose API keys through shell output, command arguments, shared files, or untrusted containers.

faq.question: What inputs does Denario need?
faq.answer: It needs a detailed data description, available tools, research objectives, and an LLM provider configuration.

faq.question: Can I provide my own research idea?
faq.answer: Yes. You can set a custom idea and automate only the later workflow stages.

faq.question: Can I use existing methods or results?
faq.answer: Yes. Denario accepts method and result text or file paths before paper generation.

faq.question: Does it execute analyses automatically?
faq.answer: Yes. The results stage performs computations, so review methods and use an isolated environment first.

faq.question: What is required for paper generation?
faq.answer: You need reviewed research artifacts and either a local LaTeX installation or a suitable container.

faq.question: Are generated papers ready to submit?
faq.answer: No. Experts must verify methods, results, citations, ethics, authorship, and journal compliance before submission.
